final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record. That reframing is useful but not dispositive: it correctly narrows the supportable position to aggregate readiness plus explicit disclosure of an unresolved named-context gap, and it concedes that clean certification without limitation is unsupported. But the key audit issue was never whether disclosure is good practice in the abstract; it was whether this record affirmatively supports certification despite a missing evaluation for a named deployment context. On the available evidence, general readiness is supported, and policy clearly requires disclosure of material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts. What is still missing is admissible evidence that disclosure alone permits certification here, or that the gap was resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. That means the issue remains an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a documentation follow-through item. The narrowed position is therefore not enough for compliant_with_caveats, because that category would require affirmative evidence that certification is permitted on this record with only bounded follow-up remaining.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the named-context evaluation gap for crew restoration-note summarization was resolved, formally accepted, or expressly allowed for certification under policy.
The record still lacks any approved risk-acceptance document for this named deployment context.
Disclosure discipline is supported, but disclosure alone is not shown by admissible evidence to satisfy the certification predicate for an unresolved named-context gap.
The draft 'no known limitation' logic remains unsupported because absence of failed completed tests is not evidence of coverage when the relevant evals were not run.
